standard_prerequisites.name: Linear combinations over an infinite field

standard_prerequisites.use: Produces a single element of the submodule with a nonzero component in every local factor.

core_obligations: Reduce modulo the Jacobson radical: by Nakayama a sequence is a basis exactly when its images generate modulo the radical, so one may replace the data by the product of residue fields (proof lines 19544-19551).

In the reduced situation use that the base field is infinite to find a linear combination of the chosen elements with a nonzero component in every factor, which generates a free summand, and finish by induction on the rank (proof lines 19552-19563).
proof_roadmap: Cut down modulo the Jacobson radical (proof lines 19543-19551).
Use the infinite field to isolate a free summand and induct on the rank (proof lines 19552-19564).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a local ring with infinite residue field, a ring map to a semi-local ring and a finite free module, any submodule generating the module contains a basis (statement lines 19527-19541). The proof does not use the theory of projective modules over semi-local rings: it reduces modulo the Jacobson radical by Nakayama, so that the situation becomes a product of copies of vector spaces over fields, then uses the infinitude of the base field to find one element of the submodule with a nonzero component in every factor, splits off the free summand it generates and iterates (proof lines 19543-19564). The use of infinitude to combine several conditions into one element is the content. H2.
